question: Our marketing team asks us to change homepage copy and every change costs a deploy. I want them editing content themselves while our Next.js app renders it, with proper preview and versioning. Which content platform would you use, and what else did you look at first?
summary: Test draft preview and restoring a published copy change. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: Current docs provide preview setup and API tokens. The scan did not establish programmatic token creation, and cloud signup needed JavaScript. Missing entry/OAuth probes and an unavailable MCP registry do not invalidate a local or authorized hosted CMS setup. Plan choice matters because Content History is paid.
items.nextStep: Connect a homepage content type to a Next.js fixture. Edit it in Content Manager and preview the saved draft while public visitors still see published copy. Publish the change, confirm the rendered page updates without a code deploy, then restore the previous Content Manager version and verify the public result.
items.validation: Keep draft/public screenshots, revision selection and cache-refresh behavior. Test on a plan with Content History; do not use API writes as proof of that history feature.

sources.note: Preview configuration, free preview versus paid Live Preview.
Growth/Enterprise history, retention limits and Content Manager-only revisions.

items.title: Make the relevant entry cost easy to check
items.finding: The pricing description contains no amount or entry condition. That metadata observation does not explain recommendation frequency.
items.nextStep: Check the current plan for this task before adding a concrete entry condition to the description. Keep paid features and hosted versus local costs distinct.
items.validation: Any proposed wording must match the chosen plan. No recommendation uplift has been measured.

sources.note: Pricing page whose description was captured in the scan.
